Subject: Subprocessor compliance pack and country mapping request

Hi Jordan,

Hope you’re well — we’re moving into the procurement review for Redwood and need a few items to complete our security checklist and legal review:

- A current roster of subprocessors (name, primary function, country/region where processing occurs)
- SOC 2 Type II report summary or attestation and date range
- KMS/HSM provider and whether keys are customer-managed or Redwood-managed (and any certs if available)
- Confirmation of whether any logs or telemetry that contain EU personal data are routed outside the EU or processed in non-EU jurisdictions

We’re trying to close paperwork by next Tuesday (2026-05-18). Can you provide the pack or an estimated delivery ETA? If you need a DPA amendment executed we can route that quickly — I can share a DocuSign.

Thanks,
Sara Lopez
Information Security Lead
Northwind Analytics

Hi Sara — thanks, Jordan. Attaching the roster and a short summary here. High-level points first, then attachments and a quick mapping.

High level:
- Subprocessor roster (attached: redwood_subprocessor_roster_20260511.csv) includes vendor name, primary processing purpose, geographic processing region, and whether they are used for production or telemetry/logging.
- SOC 2: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report covering 2024-07-01 through 2025-06-30; attached is a 2-page summary (soc2-type-ii-summary-2025.pdf). Full report available under NDA — let us know if you need it.
- KMS/HSM: By default Redwood uses a HSM-backed KMS (VaultCorp HSM cluster, region us-east-1) for platform-managed keys. We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS or GCP KMS; customers can elect that during onboarding. We do not hold private customer key material for CMKs if CMK flow is selected.
- Logs/telemetry: We separate application logs and telemetry; EU personal-data-containing logs are retained in-region where possible and routed to EU logging endpoints when a customer elects EU residency. Outbound transfers only occur for non-personal aggregate telemetry or if a customer elects multi-region operations. See CSV mapping for per-subprocessor notes.

Attachments included:
- redwood_subprocessor_roster_20260511.csv (CSV: vendor,role,primary-country,processing-types,notes)
- soc2-type-ii-summary-2025.pdf (2-page summary; redactions applied)

Quick mapping notes (excerpt):
- VaultCorp (KMS/HSM provider) — primary infra in US; key material for default Redwood-managed keys is stored in HSMs in us-east-1. Customer-managed keys are possible and recommended if you require EU key residency.
- EdgeLoggers Inc. (log aggregation) — processes ingestion in eu-west-1 and us-east-1 depending on tenant config; for EU-resident accounts we route to eu-west-1 only.
- CDNPartner Ltd. — edge cache only; no persistent customer PII stored.

If you need certificates for VaultCorp’s HSM or a statement from our infra team, we can request a vendor attestation. Also: Kimberly, can you confirm whether a short DPA amendment template would be sufficient for Northwind (DocuSign) or if legal prefers redlines?

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Security Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_subprocessor_roster_20260511.csv; soc2-type-ii-summary-2025.pdf

Thanks Mina — that looks useful. A couple quick follow-ups:

1) We need an attestation or certificate that the VaultCorp HSM cluster is FIPS 140-2 level 3 (or equivalent). If you can’t provide the cert directly, can Redwood request a vendor attestation and share it?
2) Please confirm specifically whether any subprocessors have access to raw EU user logs that include PII and whether such access ever occurs outside eu-west-1. The CSV excerpt is helpful but we need explicit confirmation for our Data Protection Impact Assessment.
3) We will need a DPA amendment (DocuSign) that includes the new subprocessor list for our procurement records — I’ve created a HubSpot ticket (https://hubspot.com/ticket/NA-4721) and can sign via DocuSign once Kimberly confirms the template.

If you can send the vendor attestation and the explicit EU-logs confirmation by EOD 2026-05-13 that would keep us on schedule.

Best,
Sara
